data.cultural_impact: The name Miruna has its roots in Romanian culture and can be recognized as a gentle, means 'one who carries peace and tranquility' in a woman's name. It's a name which is popular not only in Romania, but also in other parts of the world where Romanian people have migrated, and is especially popular amongst the Romanian diaspora communities in Western Europe and North America.
data.spiritual_significance: Miruna is a name deeply rooted in Christian spirituality. It suggests a woman who embodies the peaceful and harmonious qualities of the divine feminine. The name carries with it a reminder to seek peace within oneself and with others, to live in tranquility, and to let the love of Christ guide one's life. Additionally, Miruna can also be seen as a reflection of the Blessed Virgin Mary, who is known as a source of comfort and peace.

historical_references.reference: The town of Miruna was first mentioned in historical records in the late 14th century when it was part of the Moldavian Principality. It was a significant trading center and was mentioned in the Chronicle of Cosmas, a Moldavian prince.

In the 16th century, Miruna became an important center for the spread of the Counter-Reformation in Moldavia. The town was the site of several monasteries and was visited by many prominent Catholic missionaries, including the Jesuits.

modern_usage.modern_context: The name Miruna has seen a modern resurgence in various contexts, including Romanian folklore, New Age spirituality, and digital art. In Romanian folklore, Miruna is often associated with the moon, fertility, and the protection of children. In the realm of New Age spirituality and healing, Miruna is embraced as a personal name and an embodiment of spiritual enlightenment, inner peace, and self-discovery. Lastly, in the digital art world, the name Miruna is used as a popular name for illustrations and digital paintings that evoke a sense of ethereal beauty, mystery, and enchantment.
